problem: Prior embodied navigation work relied on vision alone (target images, object categories, or language instructions). It did not address seeking a sound source that may be out of sight in another room using raw egocentric vision plus audio. End-to-end deep RL agents such as A3C also generalize poorly to unseen multi-room apartments.
motivation: Humans find sound sources (a ringing phone, a running faucet) by combining an estimate of the sound's direction and distance with a memory of room layout. Home robots need the same ability. The authors argue that reverse-engineering where a sound comes from requires relating audio to the visual layout, for example going through doors when the sound is in another room, and that this is poorly served by monolithic RL policies.
key_idea: Decompose audio-visual navigation into learned perception modules and a classical planner, then replan with Dijkstra at every step. A visual mapper (key-value retrieval memory, or an on-the-fly occupancy map) localizes the agent and builds a partial graph. A CNN regresses the sound source's relative (x, y) from a stereo spectrogram.
insight: Separating visual and sound perception from path planning generalizes far better to unseen apartments than end-to-end A3C. Even the best A3C variant with LSTM exploration memory plus an explicit occupancy map (A3C V+A+M+Mapper, ~33-34% SR) reaches about half the modular agent's SR (~68-71% with exploration). The modular agent without exploration (~58-60% SR) beats every baseline, including those that explore first. The baseline ladder serves as an informal ablation: sound-only greedy search stays below 15% SR because Euclidean direction is not the shortest path, and adding audio to A3C roughly doubles SR over vision-only (from ~8-9% to ~18-20%). Pre-exploration adds about 10 SR points over the non-exploration variant. There is no component-wise ablation of the proposed system itself, and the explanation for the generalization gap is stated as speculation.
method: Multi-modal environment: 7 multi-room apartments built by manually concatenating AI2-THOR rooms. Resonance Audio (acoustic ray-tracing, material-dependent reverberation, ITD/ILD) supplies stereo sound. The world is discretized into 0.5 m × 0.5 m grids with about 150-200 cells per apartment.

Explore-and-act visual mapper: during a 400-step random walk, ImageNet-ResNet features (ℓ2-normalized) of egocentric RGB are stored as keys in a key-value memory, with the agent's coordinates and orientation as values. At navigation time the agent localizes by cosine-similarity retrieval of the top-3 slots and averages their stored coordinates.

Non-exploration visual mapper: a CNN maps each RGB frame to free-space probabilities for a local 5×5-grid window in front of the agent. These are fused into a top-down N×N occupancy map (initialized to 0.5, agent at center) with Bayes-rule updates. The CNN is trained on GT occupancy from 2 training apartments.

Sound perception module: stereo audio is converted to an STFT spectrogram and fed to a 5-layer CNN. The CNN is trained with MSE to regress the source's relative location (meters right / ahead of the agent), which is then converted to absolute goal coordinates. A separate sound classifier decides when the goal is reached and triggers STOP.

Dynamic path planner: the explore-and-act variant builds a partial graph from consecutive exploration positions. The non-exploration variant treats free and unexplored cells as traversable nodes and deletes nodes when obstacles are detected. At every step Dijkstra plans from the agent's node to the graph node nearest the estimated source, and only the first action is executed before replanning.

setting.backbone: ImageNet-pretrained ResNet features (retrieval) + trained CNN occupancy predictor + trained 5-layer CNN sound localizer + sound classifier; classical Dijkstra planner (no learned policy)
setting.training_data: Supervised data from 2 training apartments: RGB images with GT 2D occupancy maps, plus audio clips recorded for 10 random source locations × all grid cells × 4 orientations. Across all 7 apartments the dataset has 3,728 RGB images and 75,720 audio clips.
setting.action_space: discrete grid actions on 0.5 m cells: Move Forward, Move Backward, Rotate Left, Rotate Right, Stop
setting.privileged: w/ Exp. variant: 400-step random pre-exploration whose memory stores ground-truth coordinates/orientation. Both variants rely on a discrete deterministic grid, so odometry is implicitly exact for map building.

numbers.backbone: ResNet features + CNN sound localizer + Dijkstra planner (key-value exploration memory)
numbers.extra: 400-step random-walk pre-exploration before the sound starts. Evaluated on 5 unseen test apartments: 5 source locations × 20 random starts per room per sound. Metrics are the Average column per sound category.

results: On the new VAR benchmark (5 unseen test apartments), the explore-and-act agent reaches 67.6-70.8% SR and 49.5-54.4 SPL across the three sound types. The best baseline, A3C (V+A+M+Mapper), reaches 33.4-34.0% SR and 23.2-23.5 SPL, so the method roughly doubles it. The non-exploration variant still reaches 57.8-59.8% SR and 38.4-40.0 SPL, beating every baseline, including those given pre-exploration. Sound-only greedy search stays below 15% SR.
limitations: Very small, toy-scale benchmark: 7 hand-concatenated AI2-THOR apartments (2 train / 5 test), discretized 0.5 m grid, pre-recorded audio at only 5 fixed source locations per test apartment, continuous sounds only.

No component-wise ablation of the proposed system (e.g., effect of localization error or the sound regressor). The A3C baselines may be weakly trained, and the reason for the generalization gap is only speculated.
Relies on exact grid motion, and in the explore-and-act setting on stored ground-truth poses from random exploration. There is no continuous control or real-robot validation.
builds_on: Semi-parametric Topological Memory (Savinov et al., exploration setup)
